messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: Possible POP connectivity degradation detected in eu-west POP (eu-west-3). Multiple edge healthchecks failing; RTT spike and sporadic packet loss to origin observed. Paging SRE oncall.

Alex (oncall): acked. I'm pulling metrics + traceroutes now. Seeing a latency jump on edge-probes: 40ms -> 250-600ms intermittently. Dropped probes ~1-3% but some streams report rebuffering. Tagging as P1 until we understand impact.

Jamie (sre): thx Alex. Are errors spiking for upstream fetches or just user-facing? Dash shows origin fetch latency up ~3x for this POP only. No global 5xx spike yet.

Lin (netops): I can check BGP session state with our transit partners in the region. Early suspicion: multipath AS path oscillation causing route churn to a subset of prefixes.

Alex (oncall): Running traceroute from one affected edge -> origin:
```
traceroute to origin.prod.int (10.12.4.22), 30 hops max
 1  10.0.1.1  0.45 ms
 2  172.16.9.5  1.2 ms
 3  * * *
 4  93.184.200.1  250 ms  540 ms  270 ms
 5  10.12.4.22  260 ms  560 ms  280 ms
```
Intermittent big variations on hop 4-5.

Lin (netops): Confirming BGP flap reports from partner X and partner Y for our eu-west-peering ASN. I'm opening a ticket with them. In the meantime we can try: 1) shift traffic away from affected POP via traffic steering; 2) withdraw/announce more specific prefixes to steer; 3) failover to nearby POP.

Nina (prod): Customer impact: a handful of streaming customers in EU reporting buffering + slow api responses to embeddings. Can we do a partial traffic steer to eu-west-1 and eu-west-2? Need to estimate RPS we can move without overloading neighbors.

Alex (oncall): Agree. I'll trigger a canary traffic shift for non-critical routes first. Deploy-bot, can you run the traffic-shift playbook? (see runbook)

deploy-bot: Running playbook: "edge-traffic-shift-v2". Steps: create route override -> update CDN steering -> monitor 5m.

Jamie (sre): While deploy-bot runs, adding temporary edge-level prefix advertisement change might be fast — but that requires NetOps signoff. Lin, can you coordinate with partner TAC to confirm whether announcing /24 more specifics will be accepted?

Lin (netops): Reached partner TAC (ref INC-9876). They see intermittent eBGP route withdrawals from one of their upstreams. They've isolated a misconfiguration from downstream peer causing AS path oscillation. Their mitigation ETA: 12-18 minutes to push stable filters. Meanwhile they advise we avoid flapping our own announcements.

Alex (oncall): Okay no prefix flips from our side. We'll proceed with CDN steering instead. deploy-bot: proceed with non-critical route overrides only. Keep origin fetch load guarded.

deploy-bot: Applied override for edge-service:cache-miss -> steer 35% away from eu-west-3 to eu-west-1 and eu-west-2. Monitoring.

Alex (oncall): Monitoring metrics: latency tail improved on steered flows within 60s. User complaints dropping from 15 -> 4 in last 10m.

Jamie (sre): Observed origin fetch queue length decreased on nearby POPs — good. Adding circuit-breaker to reduce retries on affected edges to limit amplification.

Nina (prod): Is there any risk to SLA credit calculations if we steer traffic? Need to log mitigation for post-incident notes.

Alex (oncall): Noted. I'll mark mitigation actions in the incident timeline. We'll prepare customer comms if partner mitigation extends.

Lin (netops): Partner reports they applied stable filters ~13 minutes ago. BGP updates now quieting, route flap count dropped to 0. I'm seeing peers hold for >5m.

Jamie (sre): Edge healthchecks back to normal for most checks. A few residual spikes but within SLO. Rolling back temporary steering to gradually rebalance traffic.

deploy-bot: Rolling back edge-service override in 3 phases over 10 minutes.

Alex (oncall): After rollback, tail latency returned to baseline, packet-loss probes at 0.2%. Customer reports near-zero new complaints. Marking incident as mitigated; keeping P1 open for 1hr for stability.

Nina (prod): I'll draft a short internal blurb and hold on customer-facing note until we confirm partner RCA.

Lin (netops): Partner TAC confirmed root cause: downstream router bug causing inconsistent AS path selection under certain multipath scenarios. They will schedule a patch; they've blackholed the faulty neighbor for now. We should be fine.

Alex (oncall): Thanks team. Next steps: 1) postmortem with timeline + mitigation decisions; 2) include recommendation: avoid prefix-level flips during partner instability; 3) ask partners for a patch schedule. I'll hand off to Jamie for post-incident follow-up. Handoff: I'm going off-shift in 15m.

Jamie (sre): Taking over for postmortem + RCA. Added action items to ops board.

incident-bot: INCIDENT: P1 mitigated -> status changed to "monitoring".

Alex (oncall): leaving note: saw transient 250-600ms RTT spikes due to multipath oscillation at intermediate transit hop. Our traffic steering to neighboring POPs reduced user impact while partner stabilized BGP. No config changes from our side.

Jamie (sre): Logged metrics snapshot, traceroutes, bgp-update excerpts, and customer reports into the incident ticket. Will run RCA with NetOps and partner contact tomorrow.

Nina (prod): Thx everyone. :heart:

deploy-bot: Incident runbook events recorded.

Alex (oncall): handoff complete. Good work. :thumbsup:
